statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is the length of a longest nice subarray of nums. Here a contiguous subarray nums[s..s+L) is nice when 0 <= s, 0 <= L, s+L <= n, and for every i,j with 0 <= i < j < L, (nums[s+i] AND nums[s+j]) = 0. Thus: (1) there exists s with 0 <= s, 0 <= r, and s+r <= n such that nums[s..s+r) is nice; and (2) for every s and L with 0 <= s, 0 <= L, and s+L <= n, if nums[s..s+L) is nice then L <= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.
